generation_history.prompt: Use case: style-transfer / logo-brand. Edit the attached vintage CoCo computer manual cartoon into a faithful smoother application icon concept, option 4 'manual illustration'. The attachment is the source of truth for ALL hardware shapes, proportions, facial features, and pose. Preserve its visibly separate wide rectangular monitor sitting above the low sloping Color Computer keyboard body, the monitor's thin angular casing, its large left screen, the narrow right control column with two stacked rectangular controls above horizontal grille lines, and the computer's trapezoid keyboard and raised rear deck. Preserve the simple two tiny solid oval eyes and the plain U-shaped smile, with NO pupils, eyebrows, teeth, mouth fill, or elaborate expression. Preserve BOTH long thin cable-like arms: the viewer-right arm curls upward with the same small open waving hand; the viewer-left arm loops outward and returns to the small hand near the left edge of the keyboard. Do not invent generic PC hardware or oversized rounded beige monitor. Keep the reference's overall proportions and essentially front-facing perspective. Required changes ONLY: remove both legs and feet entirely; remove stray radiating marks and motion lines; redraw rough double/uneven strokes as smooth confident clean ivory-white contour lines with rounded joins and coherent thickness; orderly keyboard rows keeping its original layout, without key lettering. Preserve charming manual cartoon character, not generic rubber-hose animation. Presentation: one centered icon, square deep ink-blue background (#17344A), flat one-color warm ivory (#F4EFDF) linework with small solid ivory eyes; dark blue screen and body interiors. White lines define casing, keyboard keys, grille, hands, arms, face. No beige filled hardware, no shading, gradients, glow, 3D modeling, texture, text, labels, captions, rounded-square tile border, or watermarks. Enlarge the remaining upper-body drawing to fill the square sensibly with about 8 percent safe margin, without cropping hands. This is careful cleanup of THIS drawing, not a new character design.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the edit target: the ivory-on-deep-blue CoCoVM manual-style computer mascot. Image 2 is ONLY the reference for the keyboard key arrangement. Change ONLY the key arrangement inside the keyboard deck of image 1. Preserve everything else: exact monitor outline, screen, simple oval eyes and U-shaped smile, right control column, arms, hands, no legs, computer casing, composition, blue background, ivory strokes, existing colors and illustration style. Replace the current generic three-row keyboard with the recognizable CoCo layout in the reference photograph: FOUR staggered closely spaced rows of keys, plus ONE centered separate long space bar below them. Do not add labels or letters: represent the positions and relative widths as clean dark-blue key silhouettes within the existing ivory keyboard area. Use these exact row shapes from top to bottom: row 1 thirteen standard-size keys, representing 1 through 0, colon, minus, and BREAK at far right; row 2 fourteen standard keys, representing up-arrow then QWERTYUIOP then @ and left/right arrows; row 3 thirteen keys, representing down-arrow then ASDFGHJKL then semicolon, a wider ENTER, then standard CLEAR at the far right; row 4 twelve keys, with wide SHIFT at BOTH ends and ten regular-width keys between them (ZXCVBNM then comma, period, slash). The top number row is slightly inset compared with the next rows. Bottom row must have visibly wider first and last keys; third row a visibly wider next-to-last key. Long centered space bar sits alone on a fifth line, about 60 percent of the keyboard key-field width, with generous empty area on both sides. Keep the keyboard perspective aligned to the sloped trapezoidal deck. Fit four rows plus space bar by slightly reducing row height and spacing INSIDE the existing keyboard panel, without enlarging or distorting the computer, and use consistent narrow gaps. Preserve the ivory-and-blue monochrome treatment: do not copy the photo's gray body, red key, logo, key lettering, texture or shadows. No text anywhere. This is a focused keyboard-layout correction; do not redraw or reinterpret the rest of the mascot.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the exact artwork to edit. Image 2 is ONLY a reference for the TRS-80 red-green-blue badge colors and three rounded square motif. Create a color-treatment variant of image 1. STRICT invariants: preserve the exact composition, dimensions, silhouette, line widths, smooth line drawing, small oval eyes, U-shaped smile, both cable arms and hands, monitor details, computer casing, no legs, four staggered rows of CoCo keys with wider edge Shift keys and wider Enter key, and separate centered space bar. Change ONLY the palette and add a small RGB badge. Single square image, not a comparison sheet or device mockup. Keep the source's warm ivory drawing (#F1EBDD), including eyes, smile, contours, keyboard field, control shapes. Preserve the source geometry exactly. Only saturated colors are the three badge squares.

Use case: precise-object-edit. Image 1 is the edit target, an approved charcoal-and-ivory CoCoVM computer mascot icon.
